# Product Lens

Curated by Skill Harbor: a product-diagnosis skill for pressure-testing direction before engineering starts. Four modes: a YC-style product diagnostic that asks the hard questions (who exactly is it for, what is the quantified pain, why now, what is the 10-star version, the MVP, the anti-goal, how you know it is working) and outputs a PRODUCT-BRIEF.md with a go/no-go recommendation; a founder review that reads your README, commits, and billing code to score product-market-fit signals and flag what does not matter; a user journey audit that maps onboarding friction and time-to-value as a new user; and ICE feature prioritization (impact times confidence divided by effort) for choosing between ideas under runway and team constraints. This lane owns diagnosis, not spec writing: a yes leads to implementation planning, not more theater. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: a thinking workflow, nothing to install; it produces documents and recommendations, not code, and its scores are only as good as the project context you give it. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
